articles.title: Fumble return 21 years in the making sets tone for Fort Hill defense
articles.summary: CUMBERLAND — The play that put Fort Hill on the scoreboard in Saturday’s Homecoming game was 21 years in the making. During the 2005 edition of the game, a F...
articles.body:
CUMBERLAND — The play that put Fort Hill on the scoreboard in Saturday's Homecoming game was 21 years in the making.

During the 2005 edition of the game, a Fort Hill player had an opportunity for a scoop-and-score, but couldn't pick it up in what ended up being a 21-14 win for Allegany.

The Campers routed the Sentinels 38-16 a week later in the West Region playoffs on their way to a 14-0 season and a Class 1A state title.

But in this year's game, Ramelo Palmisano returned a scoop-and-score in the opening three minutes to set the tone for the Sentinels' defense in a 42-3 thrashing of the Campers at Greenway Avenue Stadium.

On Allegany's fourth play from scrimmage, Fort Hill (9-0) blitzed and Harley Twigg forced the fumble before Palmisano took it 25 yards at the 9:16 mark of the opening quarter.

"It was a huge play," Fort Hill coach Zack Alkire said. "That play has been written since 2005. We had a kid in 2005 that could've picked up a fumble to beat Allegany in the Homecoming game and couldn't pick it up. So every year since then we've been practicing scoop-and-go, scoop-and-go, scoop-and go.

"Melo got the opportunity today to get a scoop-and-go down by the end zone, and it really set the tone for the game and got us going."

Fort Hill's stifling defense forced Allegany (5-4) to bring out its punting unit often. A couple of the Campers' punts were shanked, which often gave the Sentinels' offense great field position.

Fort Hill's offense went the entire first quarter without running a play in its own territory.

The Sentinels' first offensive play in their own territory didn't come until the 6:02 mark of the second quarter. By that point, Fort Hill was already up 21-0.

Even after the Campers intercepted a pass in Fort Hill territory with about 30 seconds left in the first half, the Sentinels limited them to a field goal to make it a 28-3 game at halftime.

Fort Hill's methodical run game kept the ball out of Allegany's hands and prevented any chance of a comeback in the second half.

The Sentinels owned the ball for more than 10 minutes in the third quarter, and triggered a running clock with Neek Taylor's touchdown run early in the fourth.

Fort Hill limited Allegany's run game to an average of 3.8 yards (113 total yards on 30 rushes). The Campers were without leading rusher Khiante Bible.

"Our defensive line is pretty dominant," sophomore quarterback/linebacker Levi House said. "All week, we've been working (on) run fit and just having our gaps and stuff like that. Our defensive backs ultimately shut down the passing game, so there was nowhere for them to go."

Sophomore Jaiden Beck led the Sentinels' defense with six tackles, including 1.5 tackles-for-loss.

Christian Riley was second with four tackles, which included one that went for a loss.

Owen Walker contributed 3.5 tackles, while House, AJ Adams and Marlee Williams each finished with three.

"I think it's just a tribute to our film watching and our preparation every week," senior running back/linebacker Carson Bender, who was named the game's MVP, said.

"It's every week we struggle with something the week before, we're great at it the next week.

"We watched a lot of film and we put work in throughout the week and it showed out today. We stopped pretty much everything they had for us on offense."

Like the 2005 Allegany team, Fort Hill controls its destiny after ending the regular season undefeated.

The Sentinels locked up the top spot in the region playoffs with last week's win over Smithsburg. They will have a first-round bye since there's only seven teams in the West Region.

But the Sentinels could very well meet up with Allegany again the region semifinals in a couple of weeks.

The Campers earned the No. 4 seed and are set to host No. 5 Southern Garrett in a quarterfinal matchup at Greenway next week.

"We don't like byes," Alkire said. "We would love to be playing this week. The guys want to play. It's just unfortunate that the system's set up for byes. But we'll make do.

"We'll spend some time together, have a little bit of fun on Monday and Tuesday and then get back to work on Wednesday."

articles.title: No time for Allegany to sulk after Homecoming defeat
articles.summary: CUMBERLAND — After another Homecoming defeat, there’s no time for Allegany to sulk. “I told the guys, ‘I’m showing up Monday, I’m going to work,’” Allegany h...
articles.body:
CUMBERLAND — After another Homecoming defeat, there's no time for Allegany to sulk.

"I told the guys, 'I'm showing up Monday, I'm going to work,'" Allegany head coach Bryan Hansel said following Saturday's 42-3 loss to Fort Hill. "We're going to be in the weight room, I'm going to go out on the practice field, I'm going to have a practice scheduled, we're going to go to work. And if you don't want to go to work, then it's like (the movie) Friday, you got fired on your day off.

"So if you don't want to go to work with me, I'll work with whoever wants to go to work. And I'm going to work, so please show up and go to work. If you don't want to, then you're fired and it's OK. Our goal is to go win a playoff game and see what happens after that."

The loss secured the No. 4 spot for the Campers in Class 1A West and a home playoff meeting with Southern.

It will be a rematch from Oct. 9 in Oakland, where Allegany won comfortably on the scoreboard, but not so comfortably on the field.

The Rams stayed in the contest through three quarters, closing a halftime 14-3 deficit to 14-9 by the end of the frame.

Following an Alex Spriggs interception late in the third, Khiante Bible scored the third of his five touchdowns less than a minute into the fourth and opened up a 58-21 romp.

On Saturday, Allegany won the coin toss and elected to receive.

After Maddox Hensel runs of four and two yards, the Campers had some early momentum when Fort Hill was called for encroachment to move the chains.

Hensel gained another yard on the next play, but the air was completely sucked out of the blue and white side of Greenway Avenue Stadium on the ensuing play when Fort Hill's Harley Twigg forced a fumble and Melo Palmisano scooped it up and returned it 25 yards for a score.

Things went from bad to worse on the ensuing drive when an errant punt from the Allegany 45 bounced near the Fort Hill 40 and took a Sentinel bounce, ultimately laying to rest at the Alco 49 for a four-yard punt.

The Sentinels capped off the ensuing drive with a touchdown on third-and-13.

They later scored on a third-and-8, and were 3 for 4 on third down on the day.

Allegany, meanwhile, was 0 for 6 on third down.

Trailing 28-0 with less than a minute to go in the opening half, Maddox Hensel gave the Campers some life when he intercepted a pass and returned it to the Fort Hill 30.

Allegany quarterback Dylan Blank rushed 21 yards on first down to get to the Fort Hill 9.

It was the only time the Campers got inside the 10 all day.

The Fort Hill pass rush forced Allegany to throw the ball away on first and goal.

With eight seconds left, the Allegany field goal unit trotted out on to the field for a 26-yard try, but the Campers were penalized for delay of game.

After moving back five yards, Landon Biser nailed a 31-yarder for Allegany's only points of the day on its sixth drive of the first half.

The Campers possessed the ball for only one minute and 57 seconds in the third quarter and had just two total second-half possessions.

The absence of Bible, whose finger injury two weeks ago against Keyser required surgery, was noticeable on both sides of the ball.

Offensively, the Campers ran for 113 yards on 30 carries.

Allegany entered Saturday on a five-game win streak and had rushing totals of 432, 489, 402, 470 and 328 during that stretch.

Over the previous five games before Homecoming, Bible ran for 173, 243, 278, 141 and 81 yards.

Bible was limited to just two rushing attempts last week against Northern — he ran Allegany's first play from scrimmage 79 yards for a score and then had the Campers' second touchdown on a two-yard carry.

Defensively, the Campers greatly missed their 2025 Defensive Player of the Year, as Fort Hill completed chunk play after chunk play.

Stopping fullback trap was a point of emphasis in Allegany's game plan, but it was unable to — Fort Hill fullback Carson Bender ran 16 times for 128 yards, with seven carries going at least nine yards.

Immediately after Bible's injury prognosis, the hope was that Homecoming was all he would miss, but he's in serious doubt to play against the Rams in the opening playoff round this week.

Hansel said Bible will revisit the doctor Thursday, with a lot of boxes that need to be checked before he can return to the field.

"That break was way worse than anyone realized," Hansel said. "So the doctor is going to check it and, if everything is set right, looks right, and the displacement is gone, then he could have a chance to get a cast and play next week or the following week. But there are a lot of boxes that need to be checked before that can happen.

"What I will say about Khiante is he is trying at all costs to play again this year. I can't fault him for trying. I think at a minimum, it's at least a burst of energy that we bring when he's out there.

"And I think it creates at least an option that you're forcing your opponent to focus on, and maybe opens up someone else to have success. I thought Maddox Hensel played very well in the backfield, but he can only do so much. We had to contribute more today."

articles.title: Week 10 Heisman Trophy power rankings: Darian Mensah, Malachi Toney close gap on Jeremiah Smith
articles.summary: The Heisman Trophy race had a major wrench thrown into it this season when Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin went down with an elbow injury that might end...
articles.body:
The Heisman Trophy race had a major wrench thrown into it this season when Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin went down with an elbow injury that might end his season. Sayin himself wasn't in the Heisman race, but star Buckeyes receiver Jeremiah Smith was leading the race entering Week 9.

The Buckeyes had two weeks to formulate a plan for what they were going to do without Sayin in the lineup and true freshman Luke Fahey under center. What Ryan Day and company came up with didn't work, as Smith had a relatively quiet night in the Southern California rain and Ohio State took its second loss of the season against USC.

Across the country on Saturday night, Miami survived another shootout on the road against North Carolina to keep the Hurricanes' No. 1 ranking. While the Miami defense continues to disappoint, the offense is still nearly unstoppable thanks to Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

As a result, Mensah and Toney keep rising up the Heisman Trophy power rankings and closing the gap on Smith. Which Miami star is getting closer, and who rounds out the top five? Let's get into the list.

Honorable mention: Notre Dame QB C.J. Carr, Oregon State WR Jesse Legree, Oklahoma State Drew Mestemaker, Utah QB Devon Dampier, Georgia QB Gunner Stockton

The fifth spot in these rankings has been up for grabs for a long time now, and Lopez gets the nod this week. Wake Forest is quietly one of the best stories in the country, as Jake Dickert has the Demon Deacons at 7-1 and ranked No. 14 in the AP poll. At the moment, Wake Forest has the inside track to the ACC Championship Game.

Lopez has been a big part of that, and he has a redemption arc of his own after being cast aside following a brutal 2025 season at North Carolina. On the season, he has completed more than 67% of his passes for 2,176 yards and 18 touchdowns to just one interception. On top of that, he has 317 yards and six touchdowns on the ground for a Wake Forest offense that ranks ninth in scoring offense and 16th in total offense in college football this year.

After a rough night against Texas, Chambliss was back to himself on Saturday in a 45-15 win over Auburn. In that game, the star signal-caller finished 22-of-34 with 263 yards and two touchdowns with one interception. He also carried the ball seven times for 65 yards and a score as the Rebels pulled away from Auburn's upset bid in the second half. Ole Miss still has to win out in order to keep its CFP hopes alive and keep Chambliss in the Heisman discussion, but doing so would take the kind of feat that could vault him into the top spot.

Ole Miss welcomes Georgia to Oxford next week, the same team Chambliss torched twice on his way to becoming a household name in college football last season. If he can do that again and beat Kirby Smart and company on Saturday, he will be right back in the conversation at the top of the Heisman rankings.

Toney made big play after big play on Saturday night for Miami against North Carolina, which is becoming his forte whenever the Hurricanes need him to come up with the goods. The star receiver finished with seven catches for 75 yards and two touchdowns and was Darian Mensah's top target once again.

On the season, Toney now ranks among the very best in the country on the stat sheet. He is currently third in receiving yards, second in receptions and second in touchdowns on the season. It might be hard for him to pass his quarterback on this list the way that he is playing, but this pace will get him a trip to New York in December.

Mensah continues to be just what Miami needs, when it needs it. He has been the best quarterback in college football so far this season and kept that up on Saturday, finishing 22-of-29 with 274 yards and three touchdowns while running for 36 yards on four carries. His efficiency continues to be the engine that drives this Hurricanes offense, and with the shaky defense on the other side, it is the main factor keeping Miami ranked No. 1 in the country. Mensah can make his case for No. 1 on Saturday against Notre Dame.

Smith had a quiet night narratively on Saturday night while Ohio State's offense sputtered in the loss to USC, but his final stats actually came out okay. The Heisman favorite finished the game with 10 catches for 83 yards and a touchdown. He is still fifth in the nation in catches, second in yards and second in touchdowns.

Ohio State's schedule is a little bit lighter at the end of the season, but they still play against a gauntlet of good defenses in Oregon, Northwestern and Michigan. It remains to be seen if Luke Fahey or Tavien St. Clair gets the start for the Buckeyes against Oregon on Saturday, but Smith is the key to Ohio State winning out and getting into the CFP. Even though it looks bleak after Saturday night, Smith is still good enough to get Ohio State to that level.

articles.title: Oregon and Michigan set for early kickoff time at Autzen Stadium
articles.summary: Oregon will host Michigan for an early afternoon kickoff on Nov. 14 as the Ducks continue their Big Ten schedule.
articles.body:
For the fourth straight week, Oregon will get an early afternoon start when Michigan comes to Autzen Stadium Nov. 14.

The Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) and Wolverines (5-3, 2-3) will kickoff at 12:30 p.m. PT and air on FS1 in the week 11 conference game, the Big Ten announced Tuesday afternoon.

It will be Michigan's first trip to Eugene since 2003 and only the second all time. The Ducks have won their last three games against the Wolverines , with the most recent being a 38-17 victory at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor in 2024.

Oregon hasn't started a game later than 12:30 p.m. PT since its 8 p.m. kickoff against Nebraska on Oct. 17.

First up for the Ducks is a 12:30 p.m. game Saturday against Ohio State in Columbus at Ohio Stadium.

The Wolverines host Michigan State at 4:30 p.m. Saturday.

articles.title: Eagles Defense Must Fix Run Gap Before Facing Jayden Daniels
articles.summary: The Eagles' struggling defense faces a major test against Jayden Daniels. Can they stop the run after allowing 204 yards to Dallas?
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles defense is in deep trouble, and there is no time to hide it. After a five-game losing streak, the unit looks broken from the inside out. They cannot stop the run, and they cannot get to the quarterback. This week, they face a mobile quarterback in Jayden Daniels who will punish any mistake. Yahoo Sports reports the squad sits at 26th for passing defense and 27th versus the run. Those numbers are not just bad; they are a disaster for a team trying to win.

Look at what happened on Monday night against Dallas. The Eagles failed to record a single sack or even a quarterback hit on Dak Prescott. That game showed a massive hole in their defensive line. Dallas rushed for 204 yards, with Javonte Williams alone gaining more than 150 yards, per Yahoo Sports. If the Eagles cannot stop a traditional running back, they have no chance against a quarterback who runs too. Week 8 finds Washington holding the ninth spot in rushing offense. The Commanders do not just run the ball; they use their quarterback to create chaos.

This season, Jayden Daniels has accumulated 213 yards and two touchdowns on rushes. He can extend plays and turn small breakdowns into huge gains. The Eagles cannot afford to rush past him and give him room to escape. If the defense loses discipline, Daniels will run right through the open lanes. The entire scheme relies on everyone staying in their assigned spot. But the last few games show that the players are out of position and reacting too late.

Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio has a huge test on Sunday night. He needs his big men to do their job. Interior pressure must be applied by Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis to stop Daniels from escaping. The outside rushers like Jonathan Greenard and Nolan Smith have to balance aggressive rushing with containment. They cannot fly past the quarterback and leave the edge open. That is exactly what happened against Dallas, and it cost them the game. The inability to control the line of scrimmage has led to their 2-5 record.

Zack Baun and the other linebackers must hold their ground. The Commanders can mix a traditional run attack with Daniels keeping the ball. This forces the defense to watch two threats at once. If a linebacker gets distracted by the run, Daniels will run past him. If they focus on the pass, the run game will chew up the clock. The Eagles have to be perfect on every play. One missed assignment means a big gain. The stats show they are not perfect right now.

This game is the ultimate test for a defense that has failed too many times.

articles.title: Giants Miss Chance To Land Daron Payne Before Injury
articles.summary: The Giants had trade talks for Daron Payne before his season-ending injury. Here is why missing out on that deal hurts the team's defense.
articles.body:
The New York Giants had a real shot to fix their defensive line, but a broken foot ended the deal before it could happen. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that New York was actively talking about trading for Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne before the injury struck. "He was the subject of trade talks," Rapoport said. The timing is brutal for a team sitting at 4-2-1 in the NFC East. Payne fractured his foot during Friday's practice and will miss the rest of the season. This leaves the Giants with the same roster problems they faced last week.

The Giants were looking for help inside the defensive line after trading Dexter Lawrence earlier this year. They have leaned on veterans like D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris, but the team wanted more. Rapoport noted that a deal between division rivals was on the table. "In fact, we're told the Giants had interest in Daron Payne — a possible intra-division trade. We will never know whether or not that was actually going to happen," Rapoport said. The Commanders were ready to move Payne before the November 10 deadline since he is in the final year of his contract. Now that window is shut. The Giants have to find another way to get better.

While the defense lost a chance at Payne, the offense lost a key piece on the ground. Tyrone Tracy Jr. was placed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury that occurred during the overtime win against Houston on Sunday. GM Joe Schoen addressed the media during the bye week and offered some hope. "This won't be something that's going to be long-term — fortunately," he said. Tracy had three touchdowns in his last two games and is now out while the team looks for answers. Gregory Desrosiers was signed from the Chargers' practice squad to fill the hole. The running back room was already in the spotlight after the Saints loss. After all four backs dressed for that game, Coach John Harbaugh stated that someone needed to "take the bull by the horns"

The Giants lead the division at 4-2-1, but the path is getting harder. The Cowboys dropped to 3-5 after losing to the Cardinals in overtime on Sunday. The Eagles fell to 2-6 after a 27-10 loss to Washington. New York faces a tough schedule with two division games coming up. On Sunday, November 8, at 1 p.m. ET, they travel to Philadelphia, with a Thursday night home game against Washington following. The coaching staff knows what is coming. Harbaugh stated the coaching staff will focus on two games during the bye week, adding that his record stands at 15-3 in contests right after the bye. The team has the lead, but they cannot afford to slip up against a team like the Eagles or the Commanders. The loss of Payne and Tracy makes the job much harder.

articles.title: Robert Griffin III says he wants to be Baylor's next football coach
articles.summary: RG3 wants to return to Baylor, but not as a player. The former Heisman winner says he's spoken with school officials about becoming the Bears' next head coac...
articles.body:
Former Baylor quarterback and Heisman Trophy winner Robert Griffin III wants to return to his alma mater, this time as its head football coach.

Griffin, who won the Heisman Trophy in 2011, confirmed he has spoken with Baylor officials about the opening after the school fired Dave Aranda on Sunday, according to Front Office Sports .

"If I was making all the decisions, the decision would have already been made, right?" Griffin told Front Office Sports Tonight. "But that's not the process, and I'm looking forward to going through that process with Baylor University to have real, concrete conversations."

Griffin, an eight-year NFL veteran, has never coached at the college or professional level, a potential obstacle to landing the job.

The former quarterback argued that college football's changing landscape requires more than coaching experience. He emphasized leadership, recruiting and building a winning culture.

"The coaching in college is no longer about who calls plays," Griffin said. "It's about being a CEO and being able to manage not only the pressure, but also building a culture of winning."

Griffin also pointed to his Texas roots, recruiting connections and familiarity with Baylor's Christian mission as qualifications for the position.

Baylor fired Aranda after seven seasons and a 40-40 record, including one bowl victory.

Griffin, who has a statue outside Baylor's McLane Stadium, said he believes he has the support and leadership skills to turn the program around.

Regardless of Baylor's decision, Griffin said he will continue supporting his alma mater and its pursuit of sustained success.

articles.title: Shane van Gisbergen Shines With 5th-Place Finish at Martinsville
articles.summary: Shane van Gisbergen earned a fifth-place finish on Sunday at Martinsville.
articles.body:
It has been well-documented that Shane van Gisbergen has made significant gains on oval tracks in 2026. The driver of the No. 97 is notorious for being a strong road-course racer has all eight of his NASCAR Cup Series victories have come on the right and left turn tracks.

In Sunday's Xfinity 500 at Martinsville, the New Zealand native showed once again that he is emerging as a strong, all-around driver. The Trackhouse Racing earned a fifth-place finish at "The Paperclip," his best finish at Martinsville and ties his best finish on a short track.

SVG finished fifth at North Wilkesboro Speedway earlier this season.

SVG Comments on Strong Martinsville Finish

SVG spoke to USA Network's Kim Coon after his strong Martinsville showing. Piloting the No. 97 Wendy's Chevrolet, SVG was superstitious about the paint scheme being a good luck charm.

Despite starting 29th, SVG found his way to the front.

"I guess the Wendy's car is good luck. We got another top five with it, so pretty stoked with that. Just an awesome day," SVG said .

SVG said he was "pissed" at himself for the lackluster qualifying lap on Saturday. If he had started closer towards the front, SVG believes they could have had an opportunity for a better result.

Yet, the 37-year-old powered through the 500 laps around the 0.5-mile short track and ended with a quality result to show for it.

"If we started up front, maybe we would've had a better shot. Thanks to the Trackhouse team. All day, we just methodically worked forward and got in a couple little incidents, fixed it up, and got a good result," SVG said.

SVG Ranks Highest Non-Chase Driver in The Standings With One Race Left

With one race remaining in the 2026 season, SVG has the chance to maximize his year after failing to make the Chase. Ahead of the NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race at Homestead-Miami Speedway, SVG ranks 17th in the points standings, the highest of the non-Chase field.

SVG carries a 29-point advantage over Trackhouse teammate Ross Chastain into the final race of the season. With two victories this season at Watkins Glen and Sonoma, SVG is the only non-Chase driver with a win this season.

SVG failed to make the Chase in what is his second full-time season of NASCAR competition. Despite having the final position going into the regular-season finale, SVG was bumped out after Ryan Preece won at Daytona to push him into the Chase.

articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “My dad gave me the wheel, but my mom kept my heart in Bologna” - How Andrea Kimi Antonelli turned a family garage, and parental sacrifice into Formula 1 history
articles.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s rise from a young boy in his father’s racing garage to a Formula 1 world champion is a story shaped by talent, hard work and
articles.body: Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s rise from a young boy in his father’s racing garage to a Formula 1 world champion is a story shaped by talent, hard work and family support. Born in Bologna, Italy, in 2006, Antonelli grew up around racing cars, engines and busy race weekends. His father, Marco Antonelli, introduced him to motorsport, while his mother, Veronica, supported him through the demands of a racing career. At just 19, Kimi has already made history with Mercedes, but his journey began long before he reached the F1 grid.How did Andrea Kimi Antonelli grow up in his father Marco Antonelli’s racing garage?For Antonelli, racing was part of everyday family life from the time he was a baby. His father, Marco, was a racing driver who later built his own motorsport team. Kimi was just 15 days old when he first visited the family garage, where he spent time around racing cars and the people working on them.His parents, Marco and Veronica, were both closely involved in the team’s work. While his father focused on racing, his mother helped with the team’s operations and also took Kimi to race events. According to BBC Sport, she would sometimes keep him in his pram in the garage while the team worked.The young Antonelli soon became interested in everything happening around him. When he was around three, Marco brought a racing simulator home after the Bologna Motor Show. It was meant for guests, but Kimi quickly took an interest in it.His father would sit him on his lap, allowing him to hold the steering wheel while Marco handled the accelerator and brakes. Kimi enjoyed it so much that he would keep asking to drive, even when his father was tired.Marco recalled one such night to BBC Sport, saying:“And Kimi said: ‘Dad, dad, no sleep, no sleep. I have to drive.’”Although Kimi was still very young, his interest in racing was already clear. His father later said that the boy had grown up hearing engines and spending time around the family business.When did Marco Antonelli realise his son had racing talent during a Lamborghini drive?Marco did not initially want his son to follow him into professional motorsport. Having experienced the demands of racing himself, he understood how difficult it could be to build a career in the sport. The costs, travel and uncertainty made him cautious about Kimi choosing the same path.However, one experience at Adria International Raceway changed how he viewed his son’s ability.Kimi was around 10 when Marco offered him a chance to sit in a Lamborghini Super Trofeo car. The two shared the driver’s seat, with Marco controlling the accelerator and brakes while Kimi handled the steering and gears.As they picked up speed, the car began to oversteer during a braking manoeuvre. Kimi managed to control the movement while Marco continued driving. His reaction surprised his father, who had not expected a child of his age to respond so naturally.Marco explained the incident to BBC Sport:“The car had a lot of oversteer. Kimi controlled the oversteer perfectly, then I went on the throttle, Kimi finished the oversteer, changed gear, and went.”He also explained why he decided to stop the drive.“I said: ‘OK, stop, because it has now become dangerous.’”After watching the video of the drive, Marco began to understand that his son might have a special ability behind the wheel. The experience did not guarantee a future in Formula 1, but it gave the family a reason to take his interest more seriously.How did Veronica Pomaro support Andrea Kimi Antonelli throughout his racing journey?While Marco helped Kimi develop his driving skills, his mother, Veronica Pomaro, played an important role away from the track. She helped manage the demands of a racing schedule and made sure her son had support outside motorsport.Travelling for karting events and junior racing meant that family life often revolved around competitions. Kimi also had to balance school with the time he spent on the track. His parents made education an important part of his upbringing, even as his racing career began to demand more attention.Kimi has spoken openly about how much his parents have done for him. In an interview published by Formula 2, he said:“I wouldn’t be here without them. There are a lot of people that are involved in the process and are helping me, but they are the main ones. First of all, the introduced me into the world of motorsport and helped me overcome every difficult situation since.”He also spoke about the different ways his parents supported him, particularly during the difficult parts of his career.“My mum always used to bring me to the races, she’s been through those really tough moments and always been there for me as well, so I’m really grateful to them as without them, I wouldn’t be where I am now.”For Kimi, their contribution went beyond helping him become a better driver. He credited them with teaching him how to handle success and setbacks.“Not only because they’ve helped me develop myself as a driver, but as a person as well. They’ve taught me to always stay humble and work really hard because things never come easy. You have to work hard to achieve them. So, they’re a big influence on me.”How did Mercedes, Lewis Hamilton’s seat and Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s rise lead to F1 history?Kimi’s progress through karting eventually brought him to the attention of Mercedes. He joined the team’s junior programme in April 2019, aged 12, after winning several important karting titles.His success continued in the junior categories. He won the Italian and German Formula 4 championships in 2022, followed by the Formula Regional European Championship in 2023. He then moved into Formula 2 in 2024, winning races at Silverstone and Budapest.Mercedes eventually selected him to replace Lewis Hamilton for the 2025 season. Antonelli made his Formula 1 debut at the Australian Grand Prix, becoming the third-youngest driver to start an F1 race.His first season brought both challenges and important achievements. He secured a Sprint pole position in Miami and finished on the podium in Canada. He ended his rookie campaign with three podium finishes and 150 points.The following year brought an even bigger achievement. In 2026, Antonelli won his first Grand Prix in China and followed it with another victory in Japan. He also went on to win the Italian Grand Prix at Monza, adding to his growing list of achievements.His 16th podium of the season in Mexico City secured the 2026 world championship. At 19, he became the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history, achieving something that few drivers have managed at such an early age.His success has also given Italian motorsport a new world champion to celebrate. However, behind the results and records is the same family that supported him when he was a baby in the garage.Kimi has repeatedly credited his parents for helping him reach Formula 1. Their support started with taking him to race events and encouraging his interest in driving. It continued through the junior categories and into his career with Mercedes.For Marco and Veronica, the journey began long before the world started watching their son race. They were there when he first held a steering wheel, when he began competing in karting and when he took his first steps towards Formula 1. His world championship is the biggest achievement of that journey so far.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk hires Drew Rosenhaus to salvage NFL career after torching 49ers relationship
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk hired Drew Rosenhaus to salvage his NFL career after voided guarantees, an arrest warrant, and two full seasons away from football.
articles.body: Brandon Aiyuk wants back in the NFL, and he just hired football’s premier fixer to clean up his self-inflicted mess. The estranged 49ers wideout officially signed with Drew Rosenhaus on Monday to jump-start his stalled career at age 28. Aiyuk has not played a down since blowing out his knee against Kansas City in October 2024. From that moment on, he did everything possible to destroy whatever leverage he had left. After San Francisco voided roughly $27 million in contract guarantees in July 2025 when Aiyuk skipped mandatory team rehab sessions, he stopped showing up entirely. The team placed him on the reserve/left squad and reserve/did not report lists. RODDY WHITE QUESTIONS 49ERS’ HANDLING OF BRANDON AIYUK AS RECEIVER'S FUTURE IN SAN FRANCISCO REMAINS UNCLEAR Over the summer, Aiyuk took his grievances to social media, tried to force his release, and demanded a trade. Aiyuk openly campaigned to join former Arizona State teammate Jayden Daniels in Washington. Aiyuk also faced an arrest warrant in June 2026 after posting a clip of himself hitting 104 mph in a 40 zone outside Levi's Stadium. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! San Francisco never blinked. John Lynch and Kyle Shanahan made it clear Aiyuk is done in the Bay Area. Asked in September 2026 if wide receiver injuries might force a reunion, Shanahan needed just one word: "No." Washington slammed the door shut too, signing Stefon Diggs and killing Aiyuk's dream reunion with Daniels. BRANDON AIYUK SHOUTS OUT COMMANDERS IN LATEST SOCIAL MEDIA VIDEO AS 49ERS TRADE SAGA DRAGS ON Before any transaction can materialize, Aiyuk needs formal league reinstatement before the 49ers can cut or trade him. That is where Rosenhaus comes in. NFL GREAT STEVE SMITH SR SAYS HE HAS 'NO DAMN IDEA' WHAT'S GOING ON WITH EMBATTLED 49ERS STAR BRANDON AIYUK When a player burns his bridges, he is the cleanup guy brought in to save what is left of a career. His resume includes Terrell Owens doing driveway push-ups in 2005 while Rosenhaus repeatedly told reporters, "next question." He represented Antonio Brown through erratic exits across multiple franchises, and briefly took on Johnny Manziel before severing ties over rehab conditions. Aiyuk had elite production in 2023, posting 1,342 receiving yards. But talent only protects a player for so long when matched with prolonged drama, missed rehab, and two full seasons away from contact. San Francisco holds his rights without paying him a dime. Rosenhaus has pulled off miracles with troubled receivers before, but Aiyuk wrote the book on how to alienate front offices across the league. articles.title: Angel Reese steps back from 'Unapologetically Angel' podcast after Atlanta Dream's Finals loss
articles.summary: Angel Reese announced a six-month break from her "Unapologetically Angel" podcast after the Atlanta Dream fell to the Golden State Valkyries.
articles.body: Angel Reese is logging off. Well, mostly. After the Atlanta Dream dropped Game 7 of the WNBA Finals to the Golden State Valkyries, the forward announced a six-month break from her podcast. Reese took to social media to tell followers she is stepping away from "Unapologetically Angel." She made it clear that she needs to dedicate the offseason to herself. Reese is heading to Florida for the break to spend time with her boyfriend, Orlando Magic center Wendell Carter Jr. The rest of the plan is to rest, lift weights, build her brand and find "peace." Over the past year, Reese used the mic to complain that her WNBA salary could not cover her $8,000 monthly rent, lectured Cam Newton on why men must pay every bill, and took routine swipes at Caitlin Clark fans. The feed never lacked for eye-rolls. The media break follows a rough finish on the court. Atlanta reached the finals for the first time since 2013, but the Dream dropped Game 7, 68-63. Reese struggled to score during the elimination game. She logged 33 minutes but managed only eight points on 3-for-7 shooting. She grabbed 12 rebounds but gave away four turnovers. Over the seven-game series, she coughed up the ball 27 times, setting a WNBA Finals record. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! After dropping Game 7, she declared she had "nothing to hang my head about." Naturally, out came the playbook: every defeat is a lesson, a championship is "delayed, not denied," and she wants more. It was textbook deflection. CASUAL BASKETBALL FANS GOBSMACKED AT HORRIBLE ANGEL REESE HIGHLIGHTS FROM AN ACTUAL WNBA FINALS GAME The Dream front office might prefer an appetite for ball security. For the next six months, the basketball world gets a welcome breather from her weekly studio declarations. Reese claims she will return to work after her Florida stay. articles.title: Why India's 99th Grandmaster had to do it twice: The latest mystery of Indian chess, VS Rathanvel
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Last July, the congratulations arrived all at once.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Last July, the congratulations arrived all at once. Reports and chess pages across India carried the same news that VS Rathanvel, a 25-year-old from Coimbatore, had crossed 2500 at the Guwahati Smart City International Open and become the country's 99th Grandmaster (GM). It looked as if his four-year wait had just ended.Rathanvel had finished his norms by 2022. What he lacked was a FIDE standard rating of 2500. Throughout this period, he had been stuck in the high 2490s, and by his own count had reached the edge of 2500 "probably 3-4 times"."You know that feel where you know you're worthy of it, but somehow you're not still getting there," Rathanvel had told TimesofIndia.com after what he, along with many others, believed would be the moment he finally secured the GM title.Then, the August rating list came out, and surprisingly, his rating hadn't improved. With his rating still below 2500, Rathanvel was still not a Grandmaster.What went wrong?In the month of July, Rathanvel, rated 2492 at that time, had gone to Assam, needing eight points in FIDE standard ratings to meet the criteria of becoming a Grandmaster.He played two back-to-back opens in Assam, the Ayodhana International (six games) and the Guwahati Smart City Open (five), seeded first and second.Nevertheless, he didn't play all the games there. He took zero-point byes in some rounds, which kept his score low and kept the Swiss pairings feeding him lower-rated opponents.He won all 11 games, with ten of his opponents rated between 1451 and 1625 and one unrated.Each win against the rated players was worth only +0.8 because FIDE caps the rating gap at 400 points, and ten of them added up to exactly the eight points he needed to go from 2492 to 2500.In Ayodhana International, he skipped four rounds. And in Guwahati Smart City Open, he chose not to participate in five games. It was perhaps a smart move from Rathanvel.His performance ratings in the two events, 2225 and 2299, were both below his own rating as he finished 77th and 246th in those tournaments, respectively. But a top finish was never on the agenda, as he just needed eight points to qualify for the GM title.He had achieved it, and it felt as if India had gotten its 99th GM.The strange part and FIDE's stance on titles Both tournaments were rated. Together, over 400 participants each at Ayodhana and Guwahati Open had their ratings updated. Rathanvel's rating, however, stayed the same.Unlike the Tamil Nadu-based player, his opponents were in the updated rating list, but each of them had one game fewer than they actually played against rated opponents, the missing game being the one against Rathanvel.Therefore, it can be concluded that all games played in those tournaments were counted, except for those involving Rathanvel."I have no idea (why it happened)," Rathanvel told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction. "FIDE and the Indian Chess Federation (AICF) may have even had some discussion. I am not sure what happened. I was also not able to get satisfactory responses."The current rules follow the FIDE Title Regulations effective from 1 January 2024, published in the FIDE Handbook under the Qualification Commission’s International Title Regulations, in the section on norm-based titles (clause 1.4).Clause 1.4.2 lists what FIDE refuses to count towards a title. Games against opponents who do not belong to FIDE federations do not count (players with the “FID” federation are accepted but are not treated as foreign players). Games against unrated players who score zero against rated opponents in round robins do not count. Neither do games decided by forfeit, adjudication or any means other than over-the-board play, although other games, once started, are counted.A whole tournament can also be thrown out if “changes are made which have the effect of benefitting one or more players”, for example by altering the number of rounds, or the order of rounds, or “providing particular opponents, not otherwise participating in the event”.The formats allowed in title tournaments are Swiss, round robin, double round robin and knockout, and any other format needs the prior approval of the Qualification Commission Chairperson. The Qualification Commission is described as the “final judging unit” for titles, so it decides whether a result falls under any of these.The weight of an announcement The news was out that he was India's 99th GM, while, in reality, FIDE didn't approve it. "People had already made an announcement that I was the 99th GM," he added. "Every media channel covered it."There was no neat way to handle that."If people say that you achieved something, and suddenly they also say that it's not yours," he recalled. "Pressure was obviously there, probably even much more considering the circumstances."Even when he knew he had to chase the 2500 rating again, the situation did not help him in his game either."Strength was obviously there, but my mindset was not in a perfect state. A lot of pressure and other things happening around it, it was very difficult to focus," he admitted.What helped was a mentor, whose name he chose not to share."Luckily I managed to find a very nice mentor, and somehow he managed to put me on the right track." Asked to name him, Rathanvel laughed it off: "I'd like to keep him secret for a while."Doing it again The only way to settle things was on the board, all over again. In October, he played the 22nd Chefchaouen International Open in Morocco and won the title there, finishing unbeaten on 7/9 with five wins and four draws.He beat Grandmasters like Deep Sengupta and David Larino Nieto along the way.Round seven, against Larino Nieto, was the one that counted."I knew that if I win against Larino in Round 7, I will be very close to 2500, probably 2499.7 or something," he added. "And they consider 2499.7 as 2500. So I managed to win him, and eventually I crossed it."FIDE's Qualification Commission confirmed in 2025 that rating-based titles can be awarded on live ratings, but it was not obvious that a live 2499.7 rounds up the way a published figure would.Rathanvel's tournament finished with two draws, leaving his live rating at 2497.7.So he kept playing. Last week, at the Dr. Kantor Sandor Memorial in Debrecen, Hungary, he beat WFM Sara Maria Sunea and GM Attila Czebe in the first two rounds. That added 3.4 points and took his live rating to 2501.1, a figure with no rounding argument attached.His norms had been in place for years. The rating, at last, was above the line, and Rathanvel was India’s 99th GM again.Asked how it felt, Rathanvel sighed, "Eventually things went well, and I'm kind of relieved more than a celebration, I would say."Rathanvel waited four years for a number, saw it celebrated, watched it vanish, and then had to go out and earn it a second time. Strangely, the only thing that feels settled is how he feels about it. He is relieved, not triumphant, and for now that is the part nobody can take back.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: JJ Redick Makes Big Lakers Change With Ziaire Williams Back
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have made a change to remove Ziaire Williams from the starting lineup for the first time while active this season. Williams was one of...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have made a change to remove Ziaire Williams from the starting lineup for the first time while active this season. Williams was one of many NBA players impacted by the early injury bug to miss a couple of games. It seems that Williams has lost his role in the starting lineup as one of the forwards in his first game back.

Lakers head coach JJ Redick revealed the following starting lineup for Monday's game against the Miami Heat:

PG: Luka Doncic SG: Austin Reaves SF: Matisse Thybulle PF: Jake LaRavia C: Walker Kessler

Williams typically started with Thybullle, but LaRavia has done well enough to retain that spot. Redick paced LaRavia in the lineup for the games without Williams since the Lakers only have so few options to play the wing positions. Sandro Mamukelashvili and Jarred Vanderbilt will split the duties with Williams as backup forwards.

The three games without Williams saw LaRavia shooting 50% from three-point range to win over Redick. All options are flawed, but shooting and defense are the two pivotal skills needed from the forwards. Tonight's battle against Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo could see Redick trying different lineups to see which works defensively.

Why Ziaire Williams Wasn't Demoted By Lakers

Most players would take it at a downgrade to lose their starting spot, but Williams should not take it that way. The Lakers were always going to have a platoon set up at forward after losing last season's starters LeBron James and Rui Hachimura in free agency.

Williams, LaRavia, Thybulle, and others have a chance to close the game. The closing lineup is often more important than the starters since they determine the fourth quarter minutes. Reserve center Kevon Looney 's struggles also open more minutes for the reserve power forwards when Kessler is on the bench.

Redick has experimented with Vanderbilt in backup center minutes, but other forwards can be included if the opposing team doesn't have a dominant big man. Williams will get plenty of chances to continue contributing to the Lakers . Redick wanted to ride the hot hand of LaRavia and keep the current chemistry going rather than punishing Williams.

articles.title: Bills Get Bad News on Budda Baker Trade Rumors After Cardinals Upset
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills got some bad news on safety Budda Baker, who is not expected to hit the trade block before next week's deadline. The post Bills Get Bad New...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are expected to seek some help for their secondary ahead of next week's trade deadline, but one big target could be off the board.

Buffalo's secondary has struggled through the first two months of the season, giving up 25.9 points per game and allowing opposing quarterbacks to pick them apart. The team brought on some extra help and could make a move at the trade deadline, though ESPN's Adam Schefter reported this week that a stellar safety is no longer expected to move.

Bills May Need to Move on From Budda Baker Trade Rumors

In an appearance on the "Pat McAfee Show" on Monday, Schefter said the Arizona Cardinals are expected to keep safety Budda Baker. The Cardinals just pulled off an upset win over the Dallas Cowboys, bringing them to 3-5 and keeping some slim hopes of playoffs alive.

"That guy has been such a stud I don't know that Budda Baker is gonna be traded," Schefter said. "I don't think Arizona wants to move on from a guy that has meant so much to that franchise. (Baker) is such a baller)."

The Bills have been seen as a top fit for Baker. The Athletic's Ted Nguyen predicted the Bills would take a big swing to land the seven-time Pro Bowl safety.

"While Leonhard was with the Broncos , he saw first-hand the impact that Talanoa Hufanga had. Baker has been out of the limelight in Arizona, but with the Bills, the world could see how special he is on the big stage. He could likely be had for a fourth-round pick as he's 30 and has only one year left on his contract after this season."

While the Bills don't have much salary cap space to make any seismic additions at the trade deadline, the team did make a more affordable addition to the secondary. The Bills announced in October that they signed veteran cornerback Tre'Davious White, a starter for the majority of last season.

White was originally signed to the practice squad, with indications that the team will bring him to the active roster once he is acclimated.

Schefter reported at the time White signed that he turned down "multiple" other teams to return to Buffalo, the team that drafted him in the first round in 2017.

"CB Tre'Davious White is signing with the Bills' practice squad, where he will acclimate before joining their active roster. White turned down several opportunities to return to Buffalo. White started 16 regular-season games and two playoff games last season," Schefter wrote in a post on X .

articles.title: Former All-Pro Urges Bills GM Brandon Beane to Make Job-Risking Move
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills are 6-1 and coming off a 36-10 blowout of the Baltimore Ravens, with Josh Allen playing like one of the best players on the planet. But the...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are 6-1 and coming off a 36-10 blowout of the Baltimore Ravens, with Josh Allen playing like one of the best players on the planet. But their defense hasn't kept up.

That's why one former All-Pro wants general manager Brandon Beane to stop playing it safe before the Nov. 10 trade deadline and make an aggressive all-in move.

Andrew Whitworth, a former All-Pro offensive tackle and Super Bowl champion with the Los Angeles Rams, doesn't want to see Buffalo settle for another rental. In fact, he seemingly dared Bean to make a splash to beef up the Bills' defense before the trade deadline.

During a recent episode of his "Fitz & Whit" podcast , Whitworth didn't hold back with how he wants to see Beane approach the trade deadline.

"I think if I'm the Buffalo Bills, the one thing I'd love to see: stop trying to rent a guy at the end (of the season)," he said. "Big swing, to me, big swing means, 'Hey, we might be out over our skis a little bit, this might be a heavy investment, this might be a risky move, but hey let's do it like we want to get fired because that's how bad we want to win.' "Like, I want this move to be like, 'I might lose my job after it, but I went for it' because I think that's when you're going to look back and go with Josh Allen — one of the greatest players on the planet — and this team, like why wouldn't I? "If ever there's a time to say let's go all in, let's take the swing, let's go do it. I think that, to me, is what Buffalo Bills fans and everyone that wants to see Josh Allen win it, they want to see that."

"I think if I'm the Buffalo Bills, the one thing I'd love to see: stop trying to rent a guy at the end (of the season)," he said. "Big swing, to me, big swing means, 'Hey, we might be out over our skis a little bit, this might be a heavy investment, this might be a risky move, but hey let's do it like we want to get fired because that's how bad we want to win.'

"Like, I want this move to be like, 'I might lose my job after it, but I went for it' because I think that's when you're going to look back and go with Josh Allen — one of the greatest players on the planet — and this team, like why wouldn't I?

"If ever there's a time to say let's go all in, let's take the swing, let's go do it. I think that, to me, is what Buffalo Bills fans and everyone that wants to see Josh Allen win it, they want to see that."

So, which player(s) fall into the category of a job-risking move? Well, Whitworth named a few possible trade targets.

"Is it a Maxx Crosby, is it a Khalil Mack?" he stated. "… Is it going and getting that elite young rusher, or that guy you think for the next three to four years he could produce for us at a high level. I just would love to see the Buffalo Bills say, 'Hey, let's put all our chips in the middle of the table and go for it.'"

It's not the first time Whitworth has pushed a team to go get Crosby. Back in February, he urged his former team, the Cincinnati Bengals , to land the Raiders star at all costs.

Buffalo's pass-rush has been a one-man show.

Greg Rousseau, the AFC Defensive Player of the Month for September, opened the season with two sacks in each of the first three games. However, the Bills had just 11 sacks as a team through six games, and six of them belonged to Rousseau.

Crosby and Mack have both been linked to Buffalo in recent weeks.

Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox called Crosby an "obvious target" if Beane can make the money work. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Matt Bowen also both tabbed the Bills as a fit for Mack, who would be the cheaper option.

Fowler pegged his price as a quality Day 3 pick, and the 35-year-old has no money owed past this season.

Crosby is the "big swing" Whitworth is talking about, but the Raiders don't appear eager to move him after his failed trade to Baltimore this offseason. He's on a three-year, $106 million deal, and that's the problem: the Bills only have about $3.9 million in cap space, according to Over the Cap.

articles.title: Lakers player grades: L.A. scorches the Heat behind Luka Doncic
articles.summary: The Lakers continue to look impressive offensively, and Luka Doncic continues to play at an otherworldly level.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers played the second of a set of back-to-back games at Crypto.com Arena on Monday when they hosted the Miami Heat . In the first game of that set, they slid past the Toronto Raptors 131-125 on Sunday , and they once again put up big offensive numbers on Monday.

They shot 67.5% from the field and 50% from 3-point range in the first half and took a 79-72 lead at halftime. They then tightened the screws defensively coming out of intermission and went on a 14-2 run to start the third quarter and put the game out of reach. Miami had no counterpunches, and the Lakers came away with a 138-117 victory to improve to a 6-2 record.

They held Miami to 45 points on 39.4% field-goal shooting in the second half, and they continued to pour it on offensively. For the game, the Lakers shot 57.3% from the field and 44.2% from 3-point range while dishing off 39 assists, and they were able to post such impressive offensive numbers despite getting only six fast-break points. They limited themselves to 16 turnovers while forcing the Heat into 19 turnovers and they were a plus-seven in rebounding.

Overall, Los Angeles played with more pace and moved the ball around quicker than it did in its previous couple of games. Despite its turnover problems to start this season, it has been starting to look like an offensive juggernaut.

This was a quiet game for Thybulle. He made two of his six shot attempts, with all of his attempts coming from beyond the arc, and he scored six points, to go along with two assists, one rebound and one block in 19 minutes.

LaRavia remained in the starting lineup even though Ziaire Williams was cleared to play, but he had three early turnovers in his first six minutes of action. However, when he returned to the game later on, he made a decent contribution.

He made three of his four shot attempts, including a 3-pointer, to score seven points, and he also had four rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal in 25 minutes. After the first quarter, he had just one turnover.

Kessler scored 15 points on 7-of-13 shooting, and he also grabbed 15 rebounds while adding two assists and two steals in 32 minutes. The only blemish on the stat sheet for him was the fact that he didn't block a single shot, but other than that, he got the job done and made sure the Lakers won the rebounding battle while holding Miami to just eight second-chance points.

After Reaves underperformed in his last two or three games, there has been some chatter among Lakers fans that perhaps he's not the No. 2 star the team needs and that perhaps his game has even regressed. But on Monday, he returned to form, at least for the most part.

He made 10 of his 15 shot attempts, four of his five 3-point attempts and three of his four free throw attempts to score 27 points, and he also dropped five assists and got two rebounds. He did commit five turnovers and make a couple of ill-advised attempts to split defenders, but overall, he was sharp and crisp in this game.

Doncic is playing at an otherworldly level right now, and a strong argument could be made that he's the best basketball player in the world at the moment. He scored 24 points in the first half, and he never let up afterward, as he finished with 42 points on 14-of-24 overall shooting, 6-of-15 from downtown and 8-of-10 from the foul line. He also dished off 13 assists, grabbed seven rebounds and came up with two steals while committing only two turnovers in 36 minutes.

Mamukelashvili came off the bench to score 13 points on 5-of-10 shooting, and he also added four assists, three rebounds and two steals in 28 minutes. He continues to look like a worthwhile investment as a "connector" player for the Lakers.

Williams played 15 minutes off the bench after missing each of the last three games with a foot injury. He took all six of his shot attempts from 3-point land, and he made three of them, giving him nine points. He also added two rebounds, two assists and one steal.

Sexton didn't assert himself a lot offensively in this game. In 16 minutes of playing time, he took just four shots, making three of them, to give him six points. But he did log five assists and add one rebound without committing a single turnover.

Grimes also didn't assert himself a lot -- he went 2-of-4 from the field for seven points in 23 minutes, but he did contribute four rebounds and four assists.

In six minutes, Vanderbilt scored on his only field-goal attempt and chipped in one rebound.

Cameron Carr, Jaden Hardy, Bronny James, Lawson Lovering: Incomplete

All four men played the final 1:22 of this game. James scored on his lone shot attempt and made a nice attempt to rotate over to block an attempt by Ryan Conwell. Hardy scored two points on free throws, and Lovering had one rebound.

articles.body:
The Phoenix Suns lost an important rotation guard during Monday's matchup against the Golden State Warriors . Jordan Goodwin exited late in the first half with a right calf injury, and the team ruled him out for the remainder of the game.

Goodwin left with 1:24 remaining in the second quarter after appearing to limp toward the locker room. He did not return after halftime, leaving Phoenix without one of its regular contributors off the bench.

The Suns reporter for The Arizona Republic, Duane Rankin, reported on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Jordan Goodwin (left calf) OUT rest of game. #Suns," he wrote.

The 28-year-old finished with four points, two rebounds, two assists, and one steal in 10 minutes. His exit came during a stretch when Golden State was cutting into Phoenix's lead. The Suns had been ahead by as many as 17 points before the Warriors mounted a 12-0 run late in the half.

The injury is an unwelcome development for Goodwin, who has already dealt with a calf problem during his time in Phoenix. He injured his opposite calf five minutes into Game 1 of the Suns' playoff series against the Oklahoma City Thunder last season and missed the remainder of the game.

Phoenix brought him back this offseason with a three-year, $19 million contract after he became a regular part of the rotation. Goodwin started 10 of his 70 appearances last season, averaging 8.7 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 2.2 assists in 22.5 minutes per game.

articles.title: Knicks’ Landry Shamet Shouted Out By Ben Stiller For Saving NYK
articles.summary: The New York Knicks weren’t their best selves on Monday night. Taking on the lowly Brooklyn Nets, the Knicks couldn’t put the game away until very late in a...
articles.body:
The New York Knicks weren't their best selves on Monday night.

Taking on the lowly Brooklyn Nets, the Knicks couldn't put the game away until very late in a 103-90 victory.

It was the kind of win that left many fans frustrated, because the defending champs really shouldn't be letting the Nets stick around the way that they did.

The Knicks have opened the season in a bit of a malaise — some would say it's a championship hangover.

Regardless of the reason, it's a funk the Knicks will have to snap out of.

It's better to be in a funk and win than be in a funk and lose, though, and so at least the Knicks got that part right on Monday.

In large part, it was because Landry Shamet played his best game of the season so far.

Shamet came off the bench to play 30 minutes — which is more playing time than either Josh Hart or Mikal Bridges got.

The guard who wears No. 44 made the most of his opportunity, too.

Shamet dropped 22 points on an uber-efficient 6-for-8 from the floor that included 4-for-6 from 3-point range. Shamet was 6-for-6 from the foul line.

He added just one rebound and one assist. This game was all about Shamet putting the ball into the basket.

Stiller is a known Knicks super fan. That became extra apparent during their run to the title.

He often likes to share his thoughts on X (formerly Twitter) during and after games.

Stiller didn't do anything creative to shout out Shamet, but it's clear just by posting this on X that Stiller was excited:

The abbreviated version of points is kind of funny given that Stiller didn't use a lot of other characters to begin with in that post.

But like Shamet, Stiller was just being efficient.

The rest of the Knicks struggled on Monday night.

Jalen Brunson shot 6-for-16 to get his 19 points.

OG Anunoby was 4-for-10 (18 points with 7-8 FT), and Karl-Anthony Towns was 4-for-11.

Hart did shoot 50% at 3-for-6, but Bridges continued his brutal start to the season with a 1-for-7 showing.

The Knicks were lucky to get Shamet's 6-for-8, Jordan Clarkson's 3-for-5 and Miles McBride's 2-for-4 off the bench.

Without the strong bench performance, the Knicks may have been staring at a truly ugly loss to the Nets.

articles.title: Oklahoma State basketball rolls past Incarnate Word for biggest win of Steve Lutz era
articles.summary: Oklahoma State cruised to a 91-60 win over Incarnate Word as Jacob Walker stepped up in Kanye Clary's absence in the season opener.
articles.body:
STILLWATER — The first half of the Oklahoma State men's basketball season opener couldn't have gone much better.

OSU beat Incarnate Word 91-60 on Monday in Gallagher-Iba Arena.

OSU outscored the Cardinals 17-2 in the game's first 5:26. Cowboy guard Luka Bogavac made a three-pointer at the end of the first half to send OSU into the break up by 31 points.

Four Cowboys : Bogavac, forward Jordan Burks, guard Parker Robinson and senior Andrij Grbovic scored in double figures. Bogavac led with 14.

The 31-point win is OSU's largest margin of victory in Lutz' first two full seasons as head coach. It tops a 27-point win against Prairie View A&M in November 2025.

Oklahoma State vs Incarnate Word in men's college basketball season opener, see top photos

Oklahoma State's defense takes a step in the right direction, for one half

Incarnate Word scored 17 points in the first half.

The first half was a massive step forward for OSU's defense. The Cowboys held UIW to 29.2% shooting from the field and created 12 turnovers.

In the second half, the Cardinals scored 43 points

"We've got to make the first half our DNA for 40 minutes," Lutz said. "I'm not taking anything away from Incarnate Word, but we lost the second half and that's unacceptable. If we can do it for 18 of 20 minutes then you should be able to replicate that for 40 minutes. That's got to be our mantra and that's got to be our goal."

In three exhibition games, OSU allowed 99 points to New Mexico, 85 points against Tulsa and 82 against Wisconsin for an average of 88.6 points per game.

OSU's defensive effort in those contests was a point of emphasis for Lutz, who has put his energy into improving a defense that ranked No. 354 in total defense last season, allowing 83.2 points per game.

Senior point guard Kanye Clary is still out with injury

Clary is dealing with a hamstring injury and didn't play in any of OSU's exhibition games.

Monday, Clary suited up but didn't go through warmups.

"We're not going to rush him, obviously," Lutz said. "We're going to try and make sure we're as cautious as we can with being as aggressive as we can. He's practicing and some days it feels better than others and that's the tricky thing about groin injuries and stuff like that.

"Really, there's no measurement stick where you can say you're at this point you need to play. So, Kanye is a person who fought through injuries last year so he deserves some credibility and leeway here and we're going to give it to him."

Clary started 31 of OSU's 35 games last season. He led OSU with 157 assists and was second with 40 steals.

Jacob Walker did a fine job distributing at point guard without Clary

In Clary's absence, sophomore guard Jacob Walker operated as the primary ballhandler.

He made eight assists and came up with four steals.

Walker, a transfer from Sam Houston, tied both the assists and steals record for a player making their Cowboy basketball debut. The assist mark tied Kendall Smith (2017), Stevie Clark (2013), Doug Gottlieb (1997) and Andre Owens (1994).

"I think just about everything (went well distributing the ball)," Walker said. "We got guys that can make shots and it made it a lot easier for me to make it easier for them. I was just taking what the defense gave me. It was nothing special."

articles.title: It took a grind-it-out effort for Utah basketball to beat Long Beach State in its season opener
articles.summary: Runnin’ Utes manage to rally from 17 points down to avoid upset bid by the Beach.
articles.body:
There was more frustration than elation after the University of Utah opened its 2026-27 men's basketball season with a 66-63 win over Long Beach State on Monday night.

The Runnin' Utes found themselves down 17 points early in the second half at the Huntsman Center before their energy and effort picked up, and Utah handed its Big West Conference opponent a close loss by using runs of 10-0 and 15-2 to finally gain control late.

The Beach had a chance to force overtime after Malek Gomma missed two free throws with 21 seconds to play that would have given Utah a two-possession lead, but the Ute defense forced a long 3-point attempt from Utah native McCaden Adams on the final possession that missed the mark and Trey Campbell corralled the rebound to finally end the threat.

It was that kind of night for the exasperated Utes.

"I think it was disappointing in a lot of respects for me because I think we took a step back. I think we took two steps back and maybe one step forward tonight," Utah coach Alex Jensen said.

"We had three good exhibition games, but (we) can't make the same mistakes over and over again individually or collectively and put ourselves in a hole."

The Utes' coach was also complimentary of a Long Beach State team that came in as decided underdogs.

"I'll give Long Beach State credit. They came out. I mean, they played harder than us," he said. "They were ready to go from the beginning and had a good game plan and did a great job.

"We were fortunate enough to pull it off at the end, but give them all the credit in the world."

There's plenty to improve upon from a game wherein the Utes needed to complete the third-largest comeback for the program since 2014-15 to move to 1-0 on the young season.

"He just told us to wake up," Campbell said of what Jensen's halftime message was to his team. "I mean, it looked like we were slow out there. It looked like we didn't want to be out there, and that's what it felt like, too. He got on us as he should and told us to wake up, and we did."

Turnovers were a problem for the Utes. Despite Utah shooting 50% from the field in the first half, the Utes trailed 40-28 at the break.

They were undercut by 10 turnovers, as the Beach held an 18-5 advantage in points off turnovers over the first 20 minutes.

By game's end, things had settled a bit for Utah in that regard, but the Utes still had 15 total turnovers to 10 for Long Beach State and the visitors held a 20-14 edge in points off turnovers for the game, a big reason why the game was so close.

"We stress not having 10 turnovers in a game, so, I mean, taking care of the ball, hustling, this just wasn't our brand of basketball," Utah guard Jackson Holcombe said. "And I mean, we're very grateful — you know, an ugly win is better than a pretty loss, but we got a lot we got to get better at."

The Beach bested Utah at the 3-point line, but Utah manufactured more points. One reason for Long Beach State's double-digit halftime lead was that the Beach made 6 of 13 3-pointers in the first half, while Utah was just 2 of 10 from outside — and both of the Utes' makes came from Campbell.

Adams, who prepped at Pleasant Grove High and starred at Snow College after a redshirt year at Utah Valley, led that effort for the Beach, making four 3-pointers and scoring a game-high 21 points.

Utah hit double-digit 3s in two of its exhibition games — both wins — but they didn't come close to approaching that Monday night.

The Utes ended up making 5 of 17 from 3-point range, trailing Long Beach State's 10 of 25.

Utah, though, turned up the defensive intensity in the second half. TJ Burch played a key role in that effort as he finished with a team-high plus/minus of +14 — and that helped open up more offensive opportunities. In the second half, Utah shot 51.9% from the field while improving on its shot selection.

One timely steal also helped create separation at a critical juncture.

With under four minutes to play in a three-point game, Campbell poked the ball away from Adams, then quickly led a fast break opportunity.

Burch, who was trailing on the play, got in position for a pass from Campbell and hit the transition layup to make it 64-59 with 3:35 to play.

Utah ended up shooting 51% from the field compared to 40% for Long Beach State, but the Utes' free-throw shooting woes kept it closer than it should have been.

Utah made 9 of 19 free throws, while the Beach hit 11 of 19.

"Just little things like that, like the mental approach to it (that need improving)," Jensen said. "We'll get better, but guys have to realize their role and their job with the other four guys on the court and the team and not get stuck on their island."

Trey Campbell, along with Jackson Holcombe, run the ship for Utah. While the execution and effort were lacking far too often, the Utes were able to rely on veteran guys like Campbell, the former Northern Iowa star, and Holcombe, the former UVU standout, to make enough plays for Utah to eke out the win.

Holcombe scored five points and Campbell hit a 3 during a 10-0 run after Utah fell behind 47-30 just moments into the second half, and that was the spark that helped fuel the rally.

Later, Campbell made back-to-back shots in the lane as Utah tied the game at 56-all with 8:20 to play after having trailed for nearly 20 minutes of game time. That came as part of a 15-2 run where the Utes built a 60-56 lead.

Holcombe also scored Utah's final points of the night, getting loose on the baseline and cutting to the rim for a layup that put the Utes up 64-60 going into the final minute.

Then Campbell grabbed the final rebound of the game in a three-point contest, as Utah won the rebounding battle, 40-27.

Campbell, in particular, earned praise from his head coach after showcasing the kind of leadership the Utes will need this year. He ended up with a team-high 20 points on an efficient 7 of 11 shooting, while also hitting a team-high three 3-pointers.

Campbell added eight assists, six rebounds and four steals.

"We don't win the game without Trey tonight. I kind of feel bad for him because we had to lean on him as much as we did. We had to put the ball in his hands offensively," Jensen said. "And then he was our best defender on the two guys that they had that got going. So can't say enough about Trey. I feel bad because I don't think he had enough help."

Holcombe, who made a name for himself as an all-conference defensive specialist at Utah Valley, finished with 14 points, eight rebounds, three blocks and a steal.

He also tied for the team high with three turnovers, and Jensen noted the growth curve that Holcombe will face elevating his game to a power conference level.

"Jackson, no question, the care factor — he's a competitor, love it, but he has to evolve," Jensen said. "We talk about home runs or making the big play. It's like those little plays that don't show up on this sheet, like being in the right spot on the weak side and talking that help."

The Utes, who will play 12 of their 14 nonconference games at the Huntsman Center, play again at home this week.

Utah will welcome Towson to town on Thursday for a 7 p.m. MST tip at the Huntsman. The game will be streamed on ESPN+.

articles.title: Five USD men in double figures in blowout win over Mount Marty
articles.summary: South Dakota's men's basketball team started this season out with a bang, dismantling nearby Mount Marty on Monday, Nov. 2.
articles.body:
The South Dakota men's basketball season started with a bang, with five Coyotes scoring in double figures in a 95-57 win over NAIA Mount Marty on Monday, Nov. 2.

The Coyotes hung 51 points in the second half while holding the Lancers below 30 in each half.

Jahni Summers paced South Dakota's scoring with 17 points on 5-for-8 shooting. Vince Buzelis added 14 points, seven rebounds and six assists, Kajus Kublickas scored 14 off the bench, Josiah Dotzler recorded 12 points in his first game in nearly two years and Stef van Bussel had 12 points and six boards.

Ethan Kizer, Melo Sanchez, Josh Townley-Thomas and Marvin Richard III all scored five points each off the bench.

The Coyotes shot 52.8% (28-for-53) as a team, but just 32.0% (8-for-25) from deep.

South Dakota's defense limited Mount Marty to 40.4% (23-for-57) from the field.

South Dakota will look to move to 2-0 at 7 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 4, at home against Northern Kentucky.
