articles.title: Harry Kane hasn’t ruled out playing in Spain, but is happy at Bayern Munich
articles.summary: FC Bayern star Harry Kane admits playing in Spain would have been amazing but insists he is happy in Germany.
articles.body:
Harry Kane hasn't ruled out the possibility of playing in Spain someday, but the Bayern Munich striker made it clear that he has no regrets about his journey to Germany.

Kane was asked whether he would have liked to experience Spanish football during his career. The England international admitted that competing in La Liga would have been an appealing opportunity.

"I never really had the chance. Obviously I was at Tottenham a long, long time, and I was happy there, and then when this opportunity came to come to Bayern, it was something I wanted to do straight away," Kane explained (via @iMiaSanMia ).

The striker didn't completely close the door on a future move to Spain, either.

"If the opportunity arose at the right time and it was right for me, then for sure, it would have been amazing to play in Spain and play in La Liga and compete against these players," Kane added.

However, any speculation about a potential Spanish adventure needs to be balanced against his satisfaction with life at Bayern.

"Ultimately, everyone's journey leads you to a certain place, and I'm really happy that mine led me to Bayern, because as you've seen, I've been extremely happy here," Kane concluded.

So, while Kane clearly appreciates the appeal of experiencing Spanish football, his comments don't suggest that he is looking for an escape route from Munich. If the right opportunity ever presented itself, he would be open to considering it, but for now, he sounds perfectly content with how his career has unfolded in Germany.

articles.title: Oregon men's basketball shines in season-opening win
articles.summary: Oregon men's basketball opened the season with an 87-69 win over Montana, led by a new roster and interim coach Tony Stubblefield.
articles.body:
Oregon's new coach and unrecognizable men's basketball roster made a pretty good first impression.

The Ducks took it to Montana and looked good doing it, winning their season-opener 87-69 on Nov. 2 in front of an announced crowd of 4,067 at Matthew Knight Arena.

Tyrone Riley IV led Oregon with 17 points, Malique Ewin had 14 points and 13 rebounds and five Ducks scored in double figures.

See photos as Oregon men's basketball hosts Montana to open season

"Everybody was eating today," forward Taylor Bol Bowen said as he glanced over the stats sheet. "I don't think we saw a lot of bad shots."

The game marked the debut for interim head coach Tony Stubblefield, who took over for Dana Altman when the former coach retired Oct. 7 after 16 years at Oregon.

The Ducks also debuted 11 new players – nine transfers and two freshmen – with five of them making their first starts in a regular-season game.

Fred Payne opened at point guard and scored 12 with five assists, Riley was at guard, Andrew Meadow was at small forward and scored 14, and Bol Bowen and Ewin were in the post. Collectively that group scored 63 and shot 57.7% from the field (26 for 45).

They were among a group that entertained the small crowd with an up-and-down playing style highlighted by dunks, transition baskets and efficient offense.

"We have so many different weapons," Meadow said. "If we can all play together like we showed tonight, we can just keep having different guys have big nights on different nights."

The Ducks shot 60.3% (35 for 58) from the field, dominated inside with 54 points in the paint. They also had 21 assists, and outrebounded the Grizzlies 37-26.

Ten players scored for Oregon, including reserve point guard Wei Lin, who had 10 points off the bench.

"I keep telling out guys our strength is in numbers, and I think we have a lot of depth on this team," Stubblefield said. "I think over the course of 40 minutes we can wear a lot of teams out."

Montana started the game 4-for-4 from 3-point range to take a 12-4 lead at the 17:00-minute mark of the first half. But the Ducks settled in and were up 40-31 at halftime.

Their lead grew to 15 points – 53-38 – four minutes into the second half before the Grizzlies started chipping away until a 3-pointer by Jordan Clark tied the score 57-57 with 10:41 to play.

Clark's 3 was one of 13 deep shots made by Montana on 30 attempts.

The Ducks didn't get rattled after losing their double-digit advantage. Instead, they responded with a game-closing 30-12 run. Riley scored eight during that stretch and 14 of those points came in transition for the Ducks.

"It's a game of runs over the course of 40 minutes, teams are going to go on runs but I thought our guys were resilient," Stubblefield said. "I thought they responded very well and then I think we got to their legs a little bit. I think they got a little fatigued over the course of the last eight or nine minutes."

The Ducks will play their next three at Matthew Knight Arena, beginning with a 3 p.m. game Friday against Eastern Washington as part of a doubleheader with the Oregon women's team, which plays Washington State at 7 p.m.

articles.title: USC Trojans star JuJu Watkins gets emotional after first game back from injury
articles.summary: JuJu Watkins didn’t hold back her emotions after ending a 588-day absence by making her return from injury in the No. 3 USC Trojans’ 100-68 blowout win over...
articles.body:
JuJu Watkins didn't hold back her emotions after ending a 588-day absence by making her return from injury in the No. 3 USC Trojans' 100-68 blowout win over the UNLV Rebels on Monday night.

Watkins started the fourth season of her collegiate career with the Trojans, the third that sees her on the court. She suffered a torn ACL during the second round of the 2025 NCAA Tournament, an injury that sidelined her for the entire 2025-26 campaign.

Watkins prepared herself to return in full force, which she successfully pulled off. In 25 minutes of action, she finished with a stat line of 21 points, five rebounds, two assists, and two steals. She shot 9-of-22 from the field and 3-of-4 from the free-throw line. She reflected on her return from injury after the game, expressing immense gratitude that she got to come back to the court with her teammates.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"It was great to just be out there with my team again, and to see the first one fall through. It really helped. So yeah, just grateful to be out here today," Watkins said on the CBS broadcast. "I'm most proud of just my consistency. Like there were days where I could have given up, and so I kept pushing through. And I'm just grateful that I'm here."

How JuJu Watkins, USC played against UNLV

JuJu Watkins is on a mission to return to form as one of the best players in the country. She has a promising future ahead of her in the pros, needing to deliver great performances to show she has successfully come back from the severe injury.

Five players scored in double-digits for USC in the win, including Watkins. Jazz Davidson led the team with 23 points, five rebounds, four assists, and two steals. She shot 10-of-11 overall, including 1-of-2 from downtown. Saniyah Hall came next with 22 points and seven rebounds, Kennedy Smith had 12 points and four steals, while Sitaya Fagan provided 11 points and three assists.

The Lady Trojans will look forward to their next matchup, being at home. They host the Utah State Aggies as tip-off commences on Nov. 8 at 8 p.m. ET.

articles.title: ‘Matter of days’ – Harry Kane shares Bayern contract update
articles.summary: Harry Kane has made everyone at Bayern Munich proud by winning the prestigious 2026 Ballon d’Or last week. The 33-year-old joined Bayern in the summer of 202...
articles.body:
Harry Kane has made everyone at Bayern Munich proud by winning the prestigious 2026 Ballon d'Or last week.

The 33-year-old joined Bayern in the summer of 2023, and he has been simply phenomenal for the Bavarian giants.

Kane has scored 156 goals in 160 games across all competitions, and he is showing no signs of slowing down.

Harry Kane comments on Bayern Munich contract

The striker scored 61 goals across all competitions for Bayern, but his contribution to the side goes beyond goals and assists.

Kane drops deep and often acts as a playmaker. Against Borussia Dortmund, he even dropped too deep to act as a defender, making some good clearances.

He has already scored 10 goals across all competitions, and he is invaluable to the Bayern side.

The former Tottenham Hotspur striker has repeatedly suggested that he is enjoying his life in Germany and wants to win more trophies with Bayern.

Kane has a contract at the German club until the end of the season. The striker has confirmed that his deal will be signed in a "matter of days".

The striker said to the reporters : "I'd say it's a matter of days. There's been a good conversation over this weekend, and today as well, so yeah, I know I keep saying we're close, but we are extremely close now, details are just details in every contract.

"A lot of the bigger stuff has been ironed out, and we're happy with, but in every contract there's loads of little things that go into it, and small details that in the end the lawyers have to figure out. So yeah, all in all, I'd say it's more days than weeks. The conversations have gone well again today, and hopefully we'll be in a place to do something within the next few days."

Christian Falk has exclusively told CFBayern Insider that Kane's contract will not have any release clause, which can be activated by specific clubs.

Kane will sign a new contract until 2029. Talks are progressing smoothly and only minor details are left to be ironed out.

Falk said : "It is NOT TRUE: Harry Kane will get a release clause in his new contract that can be activated by specific clubs. There are final details to clear – that's what we've been hearing from Bayern Munich. But the two parties are in total agreement otherwise; Kane will sign a new contract until 2029.

"There are small details and clauses to be cleared but things are accelerating now. Before the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London, Bayern were always asking, 'Could we talk about the contract?' And the answer was always that Kane was focusing on the ceremony. I'm now hearing that there could be talks next week, and from there we could hear about a new contract being signed very soon."

articles.title: Lakers predicted to trade for $150M high-intensity defensive menace to pair with Luka Doncic
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are slowly becoming a tough team to beat. They could get even tougher by getting this defensive pest in a potential deal.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have built a new roster around Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves in a way they never would have around LeBron James. The organization believes it is championship or bust during Doncic's tenure with the team.

The offseason was a busy one for LA, as the team made several moves to prepare for the future. However, the biggest question remains what Doncic will be able to accomplish with this roster.

"The Lakers prioritized building around Luka Dončić this summer, getting him his center in Walker Kessler, adding youth and athleticism and finding players who can shoot and attack closeouts. It's a team built around a star, but are they (or is he) good enough to get them to the top of the West," The Athletic's Dan Woike wrote.

It is clear that one of the main goals of the offseason was to improve the team's defense. Defenders made up most of the Lakers' offseason additions.

"The Lakers finished 20th in defensive rating last season. This season, they believe Kessler, as well as the wings they collected, including Quentin Grimes, Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle and Collin Sexton, can provide active, disruptive on-ball pressure and length on the perimeter," SI's Ricardo Sandoval wrote.

With the Lakers looking for defenders who also have the ability to score, CBS Sports' Sam Quinn believes they could make a trade for Orlando Magic guard Jalen Suggs.

"The Magic are taking a big step -- or they're breaking up their core. They're in second apron danger as a Play-In team. Suggs is foundational to their defensive identity. He's also constantly hurt and has a ready-made replacement in-house in Anthony Black, who's headed for restricted free agency next summer. Depending on how low his value falls, he'd be a really interesting fit for a Lakers team that needs defense however it can find it," Quinn wrote.

Suggs would fit right in with the current makeup of the roster and could be a strong addition to the second unit alongside Collin Sexton. Doncic has been going nuclear as of late, so the more defenders the Lakers can add, the better.

Suggs is currently on a $150 million deal with the Magic. The Lakers' commitment to building around their future gives them another reason to pursue a deal with Orlando. An addition like this could make Doncic happy while giving the team another much-needed defensive presence.

articles.title: Is Grizzlies’ Ty Jerome the next Steve Nash? Bill Simmons wants to know
articles.summary: If you squint hard enough, Ty Jerome looks like a two-time MVP leading a high-octane offense. The Memphis Grizzlies suffered their first defeat after falling...
articles.body:
If you squint hard enough, Ty Jerome looks like a two-time MVP leading a high-octane offense.

The Memphis Grizzlies suffered their first defeat after falling to the New Orleans Pelicans by a point in overtime, 135-134, at FedExForum on Monday. Still, Jerome was quite impressive, delivering another prolific performance.

Jerome exploded for 40 points on 14-of-22 shooting, including 5-of-6 from three-point range in 37 minutes. He added five rebounds, five assists, and two steals.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Ringer's Bill Simmons could not help but compare the 29-year-old guard to Steve Nash .

"Is Ty Jerome now 2005 Steve Nash and headed for back-to-back MVPs?" asked Simmons on X.

Nash spearheaded the surge of the Phoenix Suns in the mid-2000s with his vision, shotmaking, and clutch gene. He helped revolutionize the game, making him one of the most esteemed playmakers in league history.

Nash broke out with the Suns after coach Mike D'Antoni handed him the keys. The same is happening to Jerome with coach Tuomas Iisalo on the Grizzlies , who have a 6-1 record.

Jerome is still making his case as a true superstar, but he has been incredibly exceptional for Memphis, averaging 28.2 points, 3.5 rebounds, 5.7 assists, and 1.2 steals.

While he is having a breakout campaign, it should not be surprising. He was a big-time player at Virginia, helping the team win a national title in 2019. He had a strong run with the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2025, but the team could not afford to keep him, prompting Jerome to sign with the Grizzlies on a three-year, $28 million contract.

Memphis will face the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday.
